theory.intro: The **discriminant** $\Delta = b^{2}-4ac$ determines the nature and number of roots of $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$, where $a\ne0$. Setting $\Delta$ to satisfy a required condition determines unknown coefficients or parameter values.
facts: For **equal roots** (one repeated real root), set $\Delta=0$.

For **rational roots** with rational coefficients, $\Delta$ must be the square of a rational number. With integer coefficients, this means a non-negative integer perfect square ($0, 1, 4, 9, 16, \dots$).
Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality symbol.
The quadratic discriminant conditions require $a\ne0$. Check any parameter values that make $a=0$ separately in the original equation.
steps: Identify $a$, $b$ and $c$ in terms of the parameter from the standard form $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$. Check any parameter values that make $a=0$ separately in the original equation.
State the required condition on the discriminant ($\Delta=0$, $\Delta>0$, $\Delta<0$, $\Delta\ge0$, or $\Delta$ is the square of a rational number for rational coefficients).
Solve the resulting equation or inequality for the parameter.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the value of $m$ for which $x^{2}-10x+5m=0$ has equal roots.
Find the values of $k$ for which $2x^{2}+6x+(k+1)=0$ has two distinct real roots.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$a=2,\ b=6,\ c=k+1$.

Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$.

$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=6^{2}-4(2)(k+1)\\&=36-8k-8\\&=28-8k\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}28-8k&>0\\-8k&>-28\\k&<\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}$

Dividing by $-8$ reverses the inequality.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the values of $p$ for which $3x^{2}-8x+2p=0$ has no real roots.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$a=3,\ b=-8,\ c=2p$.

No real roots require $\Delta<0$.

$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=(-8)^{2}-4(3)(2p)\\&=64-24p\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}64-24p&<0\\-24p&<-64\\p&>\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}$

Dividing by $-24$ reverses the inequality.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the values of $k$ for which $2x^{2}+2(k+3)x+18=0$ has equal roots.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$a=2,\ b=2(k+3),\ c=18$.

Equal roots require $\Delta=0$.

$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=[2(k+3)]^{2}-4(2)(18)\\&=4(k+3)^{2}-144\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}4(k+3)^{2}-144&=0\\(k+3)^{2}&=36\\k+3&=\pm6\\k&=-9\text{ or }3\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
For $x^{2}+px+49=0$, find the values of $p$ giving:

(a) two distinct real roots

(b) no real roots.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$a=1,\ b=p,\ c=49$.

$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=p^{2}-4(1)(49)\\&=p^{2}-196\end{aligned}$

(a) Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$.

$\begin{aligned}p^{2}-196&>0\\(p+7\cdot2)(p-7\cdot2)&>0\end{aligned}$

The factors have the same sign when $p<-14$ or $p>14$.

(b) No real roots require $\Delta<0$.

$\begin{aligned}p^{2}-196&<0\\(p+14)(p-14)&<0\end{aligned}$

The factors have opposite signs when $-14<p<14$. At $p=\pm14$, the roots are equal, so both parts exclude these boundaries.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the values of $k$ for which $(k-2)x^{2}+2(k-2)x+6=0$ has equal roots.
workedExamples.solution_text:
When $k=2$, the equation becomes $6=0$, which has no solution. Hence $k\ne2$ is required for equal quadratic roots.

$a=k-2,\ b=2(k-2),\ c=6$.

Equal roots require $\Delta=0$.

$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=[2(k-2)]^{2}-4(k-2)(6)\\&=4(k-2)^{2}-24(k-2)\\&=4(k-2)(k-8)\end{aligned}$

$4(k-2)(k-8)=0$ gives $k=2$ or $k=8$.

Excluding $k=2$, the required value is $k=8$.

development.question_text: Find the values of $m$ for which $3x^{2}+5x-2m=0$ has two distinct real roots.
Find the values of $c$ for which $4x^{2}-7x+2c=0$ has no real roots.
development.solution_text:
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $4$, the coefficient of $x$ is $-7$, and the constant coefficient is $2c$, where $c$ is the parameter.
For no real roots, $\Delta<0$.
$\Delta=(-7)^{2}-4(4)(2c)$
$=49-32c$
$49-32c<0$
$-32c<-49$
$c>\frac{49}{32}$
